make-bv-from-bytes-lsb-chunking: make_bv_from_bytes (native/angr/src/symbolic/bv_codec.rs) must chunk the right-aligned big-endian byte array from the LSB, NOT the front: a single ragged top chunk of width%64 bits (top_bytes=div_ceil(top_bits,8)) followed by width/64 aligned 64-bit chunks, mirroring make_bv_const's hi/lo split. Front-chunking (min(bits_remaining,64) from bytes[0..]) misaligns every chunk by 8-(width%8) bits when width%8!=0 (65/125/129), corrupting the wide eval_upto exclusion constant so ast!=val_ast never excludes the real witness. Round-trip make_bv_from_bytes(extract_bv_value_wide(x,w),w)==x guards it; extract_bv_value_wide needs a SIMPLIFIED numeral literal (model-eval output), not a raw concat expr. Fixed angr-ph300.34. GENERAL RULE (the same bug recurred on the ENCODE side in solving_ops.rs::min_wide, angr-6cp06.45): any BV<->bytes chunking loop in this crate must emit the RAGGED chunk FIRST, i.e. size the top chunk as width%N (N=8 or 64) and take aligned chunks below it. The natural 'peel a full chunk off the top each iteration' loop is always wrong for width%N!=0 — it silently pushes the ragged bits into the LEAST-significant byte, and both min_wide callers (solver.rs, solver/z3_ast_extract.rs) feed the bytes to int.from_bytes(...,'big') with no compensating shift. Byte-aligned widths (128/192) round-trip fine either way, so only a non-byte-aligned-width test catches it.
memory-keep-write-time-test: bd prime injects every kept memory's full body into every future session unconditionally — no relevance filtering, no recency weighting. So a memory only earns that permanent cost if it states something a reader would still want in a session unrelated to the code it's about: a durable invariant, cross-cutting gotcha, or workflow/process rule. If a candidate memory's primary value is a specific file:line, function/struct name, register/opcode encoding, or other implementation detail that will drift as the code changes, it belongs as a comment at that location instead — write the comment, don't bd remember it. This is angr-memories' pruning criterion (f) (rounds/review-instructions.md) applied at write time instead of audit time, to stop producing the exact class of memory pruning rounds R5/R6 keep finding and removing after the fact.

memreplay-bottleneck-root-cause: sc_memreplay bottleneck (angr-gorvf.10, commit e6f28e7c8) — the SimProcedure bounce's dirty-page replay was slow for a reason NOBODY predicted, and two plausible hypotheses were WRONG. WRONG #1: 'Rust never clears dirty_pages between crossings, so the replay is O(crossings^2)'. Rust indeed never clears it (there is no Python caller of _clear_pending_dirty_tracking, and memory/mod.rs resets it only on fork) — but the set stays TINY: csaw_wyvern replays 48 pages across 30 crossings = 1.6 pages/crossing. A per-page content memo keyed on the owning state was built and REVERTED: with 1.6 pages/crossing there is nothing to dedup. Do not re-derive this. WRONG #2: 'the FFI page fetch is the cost' — it is 13ms of 325ms. The ACTUAL cost, measured with the callback_simprocedure_replay_{pages,ffi_ns,store_ns,sym_ns,sym_entries} counters (added by this bead, keep them), was the Python-side store: 311ms of 325ms, split (a) UltraPage.store writes CONCRETE bytes with a byte-at-a-time loop that right-shifts the whole value (self.concrete_data[subaddr] = ival & 0xFF; ival >>= 8) — QUADRATIC in store size, ~6.5ms for ONE 4096-byte page (this is an upstream angr perf bug, still live in angr/storage/memory_mixins/paged_memory/pages/ultra_page.py::UltraPage.store); (b) the real bulk — a page carries ~169 SYMBOLIC objects (8107 entries over 48 page-replays) and each generic state.memory.store cost ~32us of memory-mixin stack = 260ms. FIX (RustStateSyncMixin._acquire_ultrapage + _blit_concrete_page in angr/exploration/rust_state_sync.py): acquire the page ONCE via memory._get_page(pageno, writing=True) (writing=True routes through acquire_unique() so copy-on-write still forks a shared page — do NOT touch state.memory._pages directly) and then (a) blit concrete bytes as a bytearray slice assignment + zero the symbolic_bitmap over the range, matching UltraPage.store's concrete branch (which also leaves symbolic_data alone — loads consult the bitmap), (b) store symbolic entries via page.store(offset, ast, size, endness, memory=..., page_addr=..., cooperate=False), which runs the same decomposition the mixin would have. RESULT: 10.8 -> 2.7ms/crossing (-75%). GENERALIZABLE RULE: any engine-internal SimState memory write that is already passing inspect=False/disable_actions=True is a candidate for this bypass — the only store-side mixin with real state is ConvenientMappingsMixin, and it is inert unless MEMORY_SYMBOLIC_BYTES_MAP / REVERSE_MEMORY_NAME_MAP / REVERSE_MEMORY_HASH_MAP is set (the helper checks these and declines). Residual: sym stores are still 66.8ms of csaw_wyvern's 81.6ms; next lever is coalescing contiguous byte-granular symbolic objects or exporting only objects dirtied since the last crossing.

native-simoption-has-option:
Native SimProcedures read symex-relevant SimOptions via RustSimState::has_option(name)->bool (set via set_option). The option set lives in RustSimState.sim_options (Arc<HashSet<String>>, CoW on fork, sorted-Vec in snapshot). Python wiring is TWO-PART and BOTH are required: (1) rust_manager._add_rust_state mirrors the _NATIVE_SIMOPTIONS subset onto the rust_state via rust_state.set_option; (2) those same names MUST be in _apply_state_metadata's allow-list tuple — otherwise _run_python_init_if_needed strips them from state.options BEFORE _add_rust_state runs and the mirror silently no-ops. To expose a NEW native-visible option: add its string to _NATIVE_SIMOPTIONS (rust_manager.py) — it auto-flows into both. Members: SHORT_READS, SYMBOLIC_INITIAL_VALUES. Manager-level test accessor: mgr._rust_mgr.state_has_option(state_id, name).

POLARITY RULE (angr-c7xno.61): pick the Rust-side DEFAULT in the fail-open direction, i.e. whichever branch over-approximates. has_option() cannot distinguish 'option absent' from 'mirror never ran', so any option whose absent-branch prunes paths (returns a concrete value where Python would mint a symbol) must be SEEDED ON in RustSimState::with_solver_endian (state/construction.rs) and explicitly CLEARED by the mirror. That is why the mirror loop is set_option(opt, opt in angr_state.options) — both directions — not 'set only when present'. SYMBOLIC_INITIAL_VALUES is the worked example: seeded ON, cleared only for remove_options= callers.

FACT that misleads people (it misled docs/extending-angr/simprocedures.rst's warning box): SYMBOLIC_INITIAL_VALUES is NOT 'off by default'. sim_options.modes ships it in symbolic, symbolic_approximating, static, fastpath and tracing, so factory.entry_state() has it set and SimSolver.Unconstrained mints a symbol in the common case; the BVV(0) branch only fires for an explicit remove_options={SYMBOLIC_INITIAL_VALUES}.

no-default-features-build-broken-2026-07:
The rust-symex --no-default-features combos rot silently because ralph commits straight to the branch (PR-time rust_feature_flags_check never runs) and nobody watches nightly rust_feature_flags. Three rounds so far. (1) 2026-07-30, angr-1yge9.14: the LIB was broken -- symbolic/value_ops.rs extract_no_ctx/drive_extract called bv_codec::concrete_extract_u128 inside a vex-engine-z3-gated module, and snapshot_fork_ops.rs touched the z3-gated SymContext.deterministic / .use_shared_lineage_solver fields. Fixed by moving concrete_extract_u128 into an ungated symbolic/bv_concrete.rs and cfg-gating the 3 snapshot sites. (2) angr-cagbn: in-crate test modules referenced z3 ungated; the test_submod! macro in lib.rs grew z3-prefixed arms that expand to cfg(all(test, feature=vex-engine-z3)). (3) 2026-08-09, angr-c7xno.99: the check gates ran plain cargo check with NO --all-targets, so only the lib target was ever compiled and the no-z3 test+bench targets had rotted to 41 errors. ROOT LESSON, generalizes past this repo: a cargo check gate without --all-targets proves nothing about test/bench/example targets, and if the only thing that builds them is a nightly nobody reads, they rot for months. --all-targets is now in make check-no-z3, ci.yml rust_feature_flags_check and nightly-ci.yml rust_feature_flags. Second-order effect: because the no-z3 test targets never compiled, the cfg(not(feature=vex-engine-z3)) MOCK ARMS have had zero runtime coverage -- that is the soil angr-c7xno.77 (mock merge() skipping a length assert) grew in, and unmasking the build immediately surfaced 5 more genuine mock divergences (angr-c7xno.100). Gating a z3 test strands its shared helpers as dead code in the no-z3 test build; the crate-level answer lives in lib.rs as cfg_attr(all(test, not(feature = vex-engine-z3)), allow(dead_code, unused_imports)) -- do NOT sprinkle per-helper cfgs. RESOLUTION of those 5 (angr-c7xno.100, commit de06e70b0): 2 were a REAL bug, not a test artifact -- the mock push()/pop() were no-ops and try_pop() returned true unconditionally, so RustSolverContext::pop accepted an unbalanced pop the z3 arm refuses with a ValueError, and constraints added inside a scope survived the matching pop. Fixed with SymContext::mock_scope_savepoints (context.rs), the no-z3 analogue of bare_local_savepoints: push() records local_constraints.assumed.len() (the only local log the no-z3 LocalConstraints has -- z3_assertions/non_bv_assertions/dedup_set are all z3-gated out), pop() truncates back to it, try_pop() refuses on an empty stack, and the no-z3 fork() derives scope_open from it instead of hardcoding false. TRIAGE RULE for the rest: a mock divergence that needs a MODEL (eval of a symbolic BV) cannot be made faithful without reimplementing constraint solving -- but prefer asserting the divergence over gating the test. Pattern: 'let expected = cfg!(feature = "vex-engine-z3").then(|| ...); assert_eq!(got, expected)' (see assert_jump_pinned in exploration/core_outcome_tests/symbolic_jump.rs) keeps every engine-agnostic assertion in the test running under no-z3, where a #[cfg] on the whole #[test] fn would delete them. Full-test z3-gating is the last resort and must carry a rationale comment.

pattern-nxn-pairing-isolation-test:
PATTERN — pinning a hand-copied pairing that sits one layer BELOW a compile-time guarantee (angr-0jh0j.81). angr-macros closes naming invariants at the layer it generates (inspect_test_entries! derives py_call_inspect_<event> -> call_inspect_<event>), but the generated method's BODY still hand-reads its slot (self.inspect_<event>.as_ref()). That boundary is where the bug family recurs — same rule as the MergePolicy '#[merge_policy="delegate"] marks where the guarantee ENDS' corollary in angr-macros-call-site-invariants. When no structural fix is expressible, the fallback is an N x N table test, NOT another baseline script. CORRECTION (angr-6cp06.79): 'a macro cannot verify which field an arbitrary body reads' was too pessimistic and cost this instance a round — it does not have to *verify* the read, it can *own* it. inspect_dispatch! makes the body write self.with_slot(absent, f) and expands that to self.with_inspect_cb(self.inspect_<event>.as_ref(), absent, f), so the field is derived, not checked, and everything else in the body stays arbitrary (same placeholder-rewrite trick as inspect_test_entries!'s self.forward(..)). GENERAL RULE: before settling for an N x N test at a 'the guarantee ends here' boundary, ask whether the hand-written token can be replaced by a placeholder the generator expands — a rewrite-the-placeholder macro reaches into arbitrary bodies that a signature-DSL generator cannot. Reserve the table test for boundaries where the paired value is genuinely computed rather than named. Recipe, canonical instance callbacks/inspect_tests.rs::INSPECT_DISPATCH_CASES + each_call_inspect_dispatches_only_its_own_slot (kept as the behavioural half after inspect_dispatch! landed — the macro proves the slot NAME is derived, the table still proves the wired slot is the one the Python callback actually observes end to end):

1. Table row = (event name, slot setter fn ptr, dispatch-call fn ptr). Wire exactly ONE slot, invoke ALL rows' dispatch methods, assert observed == (wired.event == called.event). Off-diagonal catches a transposed slot read; the DIAGONAL requirement is what makes the table self-checking — a row whose setter and invoker name different events fails at i==j instead of passing vacuously. This is why one-slot-at-a-time beats wire-all-then-call-one.
2. Pair it with a completeness cross-check against whatever single-source-of-truth enumeration already exists (here InspectBit::ALL from inspect_events!, minus the 3 Python-dispatched events), so adding a 19th dispatch method fails a test rather than silently skipping the pairing check.
3. A row whose fire is NOT observable in the cargo-test interpreter still belongs in the table — give it a per-row flag rather than dropping it. call_inspect_constraints imports claripy AFTER its slot check and cargo-test has no claripy, so its row sets may_err_when_wired and counts Err as 'read the slot'; it stays a real pairing assertion in both directions.
4. Mutation-verify before trusting it: point one dispatch method at a sibling slot and confirm the named assertion fires.

Generalizes to any identically-typed hand-paired set here (callback slots, opcode maps, merge fields) — Option<Py<PyAny>> siblings all typecheck against each other, so only a test can separate them.

stat-symlink-follow-semantics: stat-family symlink semantics (angr-9ke6b.235, refined angr-zueuw): syscalls/file_path/stat.rs has two shared resolvers — stat_lookup_nofollow reports a FileSystem::readlink_target hit as st_mode=S_IFLNK_0777 sized to the raw target bytes, and stat_lookup_follow walks the symlink table up to MAX_SYMLINK_HOPS=8 then stats the final target; dangling link, non-UTF-8 target (targets are Vec<u8>, the known-path set is String-keyed) and cycles all return -1. Consumers: NativeLstatSyscall -> nofollow, NativeStatSyscall -> follow, NativeNewfstatatSyscall -> EITHER, selected by the AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW (0x100) bit of its flag arg. That flag branch is not optional polish: ARM64's asm-generic ABI dropped legacy lstat entirely (NativeLstatSyscall is registered only on AMD64/X86/ARM/MIPS32), so glibc lstat() on aarch64 lowers to fstatat(AT_FDCWD, path, buf, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) and newfstatat is the ONLY no-follow stat entry point there — any future stat-family handler that takes an AT_* flag must decide follow-vs-nofollow from it, and must treat a symbolic flag as SymbolicArgument (defer to Python) rather than assuming follow, since the two branches report different st_mode. write_stat_for_arch and all five per-arch writers take st_mode as a parameter — do NOT reintroduce a hardcoded S_IFREG_0755 inside a writer. MIPS32 is the one arch where a symlink is invisible to lstat: write_mips32_stat mirrors angr's _store_mips32, which emits NO st_mode field, so it takes _mode and only st_size differs. See symlink-table-readlink-model for the table itself.
stats-counter-test-patterns:
Testing stats.rs's process-global counters (native/angr/src/symbolic/stats.rs) needs two distinct techniques, and mixing them up is what makes such tests flaky:

(1) PURE SEAM for per-bucket emit loops. get_solver_stats() delegates to insert_check_site_stats / insert_query_class_stats / insert_counter_stats (the last named insert_measurement_stats before angr-03vl4.64), which take counts+names (or (&str,&AtomicU64) pairs) instead of reading the process atomics. stats_tests.rs drives them with synthetic local atomics, so the key-presence policies (check sites: omit when count==0; query classes and the counter tables: always emit) are deterministic under the parallel runner. Any future per-bucket aggregation should get the same shape.

(2) MARKER BUMP for anything with no seam -- derived keys (z3_saved_check_total sums six atomics) and the table-wiring tests that must prove a given atomic reaches a given key. Pattern: fetch_add(MARK=1<<40), read get_solver_stats(), then restore with fetch_update(|v| v.saturating_sub(MARK)) -- NEVER a plain fetch_sub, because a sibling test's reset_solver_stats() landing in the window would wrap the counter to ~u64::MAX. WATERMARK_COUNTERS are AtomicU32, so their wiring test uses MARK32=1<<24 with the same saturating restore.

(2a) THE MARKER_TEST_LOCK RULE: EVERY test in stats_tests.rs that applies a MARK to a process-global atomic must hold marker_guard() for the whole window -- not just the tests that READ a derived total. Getting this wrong cost two flaky-gate beads (angr-7x2ve, angr-9ke6b.227, fixed in e3f7e0ff9): test_measurement_counters_reach_their_stats_key bumped every MEASUREMENT_COUNTERS entry unguarded, and because those are real summands of z3_saved_check_total AND real emitted keys, its live marker made test_saved_check_total_excludes_ast_memo_hit read total=2^40+44 and made the ticker test (2b) report a bogus leak on whatever key was mid-bump. angr-03vl4.64 added two more bumping tests (core/watermark wiring); they take the guard for the same reason.

(2b) NEGATIVE marker bump -- asserting a counter is NOT emitted (test_simplify_sample_ticker_is_not_emitted): bump the atomic by MARK, then assert no key GREW by >= MARK across the bump window. Catches a new emit under ANY key spelling, unlike naming the expected key. It is a DELTA, not an absolute '>= MARK' scan (angr-c0wlh): the absolute form needed a name-based carve-out for _time_ns wall-clock sums that can legitimately exceed MARK (~18 min) on a long run, and that heuristic was the standing suspect for the test's one observed flake. This scan is why (2a) is a hard rule: it makes every unguarded MARK bumper anywhere in the file a racer.

Also: the raw stats key for ZEXT_CMP_TRIVIAL_DECIDE_COUNT is 'zext_cmp_trivial_decide_count' (with the _count suffix), unlike its neighbours z3_branch_model_hit / z3_extrema_model_hit / z3_eval_upto_model_hit which have none.

For the common sequential write-only fd (position starts 0, only writes) this is byte-identical to append, so NO regression (defcamp_r100 0.33s, fast-tier 20/20, rust pytest 964; commit 994707c63). It fixes the seek-then-write / interleaved read-then-write divergence the old append model had vs Python's position-aware simfd.write. The append bit is NOT carried by register_fd_at, so an fd synced in from a Python state reconstitutes non-append.
